context.clinical_context_summary: 79-year-old Female with a complex history including Sepsis, Brown-Sequard syndrome, COPD with hypercapnia, and a Stage 4 sacral pressure ulcer. Medications include Atorvastatin and nutritional supplements, with a history of anticoagulant use. Presents with Blood Infection. Patient demonstrates significant baseline hypotension (Mean SBP 80 mmHg) and hypothermia (Mean Temp 34.7°C), requiring adjusted monitoring thresholds to detect septic shock progression.
context.rationale: Thresholds are significantly adjusted for baseline hypotension (Mean SBP 80) and hypothermia (Mean 34.7°C), likely due to sepsis, spinal cord injury, or axillary measurement; standard alarms would be non-informative. The fever threshold is lowered to 37.2°C to detect relative temperature spikes in this hypothermic context. HR thresholds remain standard to detect septic tachycardia. SpO2 low threshold is set to 90% accommodating COPD history while maintaining safety.
